# Plan: Build the opening environment and terminal

## Design

Source context: `index.html` has `#app` and loads `src/main.ts`; `three` is in `package.json`; `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts` serves the build under `/signal-lost/`; `.swarm/architecture.md` names the `app`, `render`, `terminal`, and `input` modules.

- `src/app/scenes.ts`: DOM-free `createSceneManager()`. A `Scene` has `mount(): void` and `dispose(): void`. `show(scene)` disposes the current scene before mounting the next one; `dispose()` tears down the current one. Pure, unit-tested.
- `src/app/opening.ts`: opening scene. Prints the opening screen's lines one by one, then the prompt. Enter or a click at any time moves on. Removes its listeners on dispose.
- `src/app/hub.ts`: boot sequence and terminal hub. Prints the boot screen's lines, then a numbered tool menu from a `Tool[]` list. Tools are `{ id, label, run }`. This WorkUnit ships only real ones (`STATUS`, `HELP`); later WorkUnits add theirs. No placeholder entries.
- `src/terminal/terminal.ts`: DOM terminal. `print(lines)`, `menu(items)`, and a command input. Output goes in a `role="log"` `aria-live="polite"` element as real text. Menu items are buttons, also chosen by typing the number or name.
- `src/render/environment.ts`: Three.js scene, loaded by dynamic import so text appears before the 3D code does. Starfield `Points`, a flat-shaded low-poly icosahedron with a ring, a moving analyzer sweep line, low-resolution rendering with pixelated CSS scaling, vertex snapping by `onBeforeCompile`. `createEnvironment(canvas, { motion })` returns `{ start, stop, setMotion, dispose }`, or throws when WebGL is unavailable. Rendering stops when the document is hidden and on `stop`/`dispose`, which also disposes geometries, materials and the renderer. `motion: false` renders one still frame.
- `src/main.ts`: bootstraps. If the environment throws, it sets `document.body.dataset.render = 'fallback'` and shows a CSS-only static starfield; otherwise `'webgl'`. The game continues either way.
- `src/style.css`: CRT bezel, amber phosphor, subtle scanlines and vignette, and periodic interference as a CSS animation on an overlay. System monospace stack, because no font asset is in the repo.

## Text

The opening and boot blocks are declarative content, in `content/screens/opening.json` and `content/screens/boot.json`. This needs a small new content kind, `screens` (`id`, `lines[]`), added to `src/content/schema.ts` and `validate.ts` and read through `loadBundledContent`. Fixed labels such as HELP and STATUS stay in source. All of the copy below is proposed here for maintainer review on the PR; the WorkUnit itself requires only `SIGNAL RECEIVED` and `PRESS ENTER TO JOIN THE NETWORK`.

Opening:

    SIGNAL RECEIVED
    ORIGIN: UNKNOWN
    CLASSIFICATION: UNRESOLVED
    CONFIDENCE: 0.0031%

    ADDITIONAL OBSERVERS REQUIRED.

    PRESS ENTER TO JOIN THE NETWORK

Boot:

    OBSERVER NETWORK CLIENT 2.3
    CHECKING WORK QUEUE ......... 1 UNIT
    PEERS REACHABLE ............. 0
    SYSTEM CLOCK ................ 2001
    TOOLS AVAILABLE TO THIS OBSERVER:

## Lifecycle ownership

- `main.ts` owns the one render host for the whole session. It creates it once and disposes it on `pagehide`. Scenes never create or dispose the renderer. They only choose its layout through `document.body.dataset.scene` (`opening`, `hub`), which CSS uses to size the canvas; a `ResizeObserver` in `environment.ts` tracks the result.
- `src/render/host.ts` (DOM-free): `createRenderHost(load)` calls an injected async loader. If `dispose()` happens before the import resolves, the environment is disposed as soon as it arrives and never started. Load failure calls `onFailure`, which `main.ts` uses for the fallback.
- `src/render/loop.ts` (DOM-free): `createLoop({ draw, schedule, cancel })` with `start`, `stop`, `setMotion`, `setVisible`, `dispose`. No frame is scheduled when stopped, hidden, motion-off, or disposed. Motion-off draws one still frame.
- Scenes own their own timers and listeners, cleared in `dispose`. The `Terminal` is owned by whichever scene mounted it.

## Files

New: `content/screens/{opening,boot}.json`, `src/app/{scenes,opening,hub}.ts`, `src/render/{host,loop}.ts`, `src/terminal/terminal.ts`, `src/render/environment.ts`, `src/style.css`, `tests/unit/{scenes,render}.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts`. Changed: `src/content/{schema,validate}.ts`, `tests/unit/content.test.ts`, `src/main.ts`, `index.html` only if the stylesheet link needs it, `tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts` (the old text expectation still applies), `playwright.config.ts` (add a software WebGL launch flag so tests can exercise the real renderer).

## Edge cases

- Enter pressed before the opening finishes still boots.
- WebGL failing at context creation shows the fallback with no uncaught error.
- A dynamic-import or render failure also uses the fallback.
- Resizing updates the renderer size.

## Out of scope

Puzzles, audio, persistence, settings UI.

# Test plan

| Acceptance criterion | Verification | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Opening shows starfield, rotating object, sweep, interference and the text, ending in the prompt | `tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts`: text and prompt visible, `body[data-render=webgl]`, canvas has non-blank pixels, interference overlay present. Source inspection: rotation updates per frame, sweep position moves per frame, the interference CSS animation repeats, and the renderer uses a pixel ratio below 1 with `image-rendering: pixelated`. The exact opening text sequence is asserted. | Developer on host; CI `Browser tests` |
| Enter or click boots into a terminal with a tool menu | `opening.spec.ts`, once with Enter and once with click, then a menu button works and a typed command works | Developer on host; CI |
| WebGL failure shows a styled fallback and stays playable | `opening.spec.ts` forces `getContext` to return null by init script: `data-render=fallback`, no page errors, boot works, then a menu button and a typed command each produce readable output | Developer on host; CI |
| Lifecycle mounts and disposes scenes, rendering stops when not needed | `npx vitest run tests/unit/scenes.test.ts tests/unit/render.test.ts`: mount order, replacement disposes first, final disposal; no frames scheduled when stopped, hidden, motion-off or disposed; a host disposed before its import resolves never starts | Developer; tester inspects |
| Browser tests cover opening, boot, fallback under the subpath | `fixtures.ts` returns 404 outside `/signal-lost/`; `opening.spec.ts` uses it | CI |

The opening spec's exact text assertion also proves `content/screens` loads under `/signal-lost/`. A `content.test.ts` case covers the `screens` kind.

Browser or source checks also cover: `role=log` with `aria-live=polite`, output as DOM text, keyboard focus on the command input after boot, and visible focus styles on the menu and input.

Browser command: `npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/opening.spec.ts`. It runs on the host and in CI, never as a sandbox implementation dependency.

## Roles

- **Developer:** runs focused commands above and `npm run lint`. Browser specs run on the host session, as sandboxes cannot start Chromium (`.swarm/rules/lessons.md`).
- **Tester:** independently inspects source against the criteria, reuses applicable passing results, repeats only for relevant changes, failures, or unresolved coverage.
- **Coordinator:** alone runs the complete required policy. The `Browser tests` workflow on the PR is the browser evidence.
